\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Deciders: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Binary width bound from a configuration code]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.width_of_code}
\label{Complexity.Codec.width_of_code}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x,y$ be finite bit strings, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $C$ be a
configuration of a finite-tape Turing machine on input $x$. If the configuration word
for $C$ with window parameter $s$ has length at most $|y|$, then the length of the
binary expansion of $s$ is at most the length of the binary expansion of $|y|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Configuration word length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_le_length}
\label{Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_le_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Turing.Cfg, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $x$
be a Boolean input word, let $C$ be a configuration of $N$ on input $x$, and let
$s\in\mathbb{N}$. For every Boolean list $r$, the length of the encoded configuration
word is at most the length of the pair encoding of $x$ with the pair encoding of that
configuration word and $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the guarded configuration bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.gd_mono}
\label{Complexity.Codec.gd_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.PreS}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let
$\mathrm{mode}$ be one of the four codec modes, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $a$
be a 21-register configuration satisfying the guard: its control state meets the
precondition for the codec program in mode $\mathrm{mode}$ on input $y$, and every
register is at most $(8W(N)+8)(|y|+1)$. Then the precondition still holds and every
register is at most $(8W(N)+8)(|y|+1)^1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound from binary word width]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.s_le_of_width}
\label{Complexity.Codec.s_le_of_width}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_le_of_width, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_bits}
\difficulty{3}
Let $y$ be a Boolean word of positive length and let $s$ be a natural number. If the
binary representation of $s$ has length at most the binary representation of $|y|$, then
$s\le 2|y|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Preliminary certificate check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.PreChk}
\label{Complexity.Codec.PreChk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s\in\mathbb{N}$ and $w$ be a finite Boolean string. The predicate holds exactly when
$w$ has length $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(n)+1$, its bit at position $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(n)$ (using
`false` if that position is out of range) is true, and the natural number encoded by the
length-$w_P(n)$ segment of $w$ beginning at position $W(N)(2s+1)$ is at most $n+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Validity Check and Its Preliminary Conditions]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff_pre}
\label{Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff_pre}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.PreChk, Complexity.Codec.VAcc, Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.vScan}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s\in\mathbb N$ and $w$ be a finite Boolean word. The validity condition on $w$ is
equivalent to the conjunction of the following preliminary conditions and the verifier
acceptance test on the prefix of length $W(2s+1)$: $|w|=W(2s+1)+wP(n)+1$, the bit of $w$
at position $W(2s+1)+wP(n)$ is true, and the integer represented by the $wP(n)$ bits
immediately after the first $W(2s+1)$ bits, read with the first bit least significant,
is at most $n+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Initial execution of the codec program]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.one_run}
\label{Complexity.Codec.one_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.PreChk, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.Shape1, Complexity.Codec.VAd, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_lt_two_pow, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.bnd_ge, Complexity.Codec.layR, Complexity.Codec.layout_run, Complexity.Codec.le_phase, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.parse_run, Complexity.Codec.s_le_of_width, Complexity.Codec.two_pow_bits_le, Complexity.Codec.vScan, Complexity.Codec.vscan_run, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.Codec.wP_le, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.length_pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let
$\mathrm{mode}$ be one of the codec modes other than the step mode. For every bit string
$y$, at least one of the following holds. Either there are bit strings $x,w$ and a
natural number $s$ such that $y=\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$,
$|\mathrm{bits}(s)|\leq |\mathrm{bits}(|y|)|$, and, writing $W$ for the chunk width, $w$
has length $W(2s+1)+|\mathrm{bits}(|x|)|+1$, has a $1$ at position
$W(2s+1)+|\mathrm{bits}(|x|)|$, and the value of the following $|\mathrm{bits}(|x|)|$
bits is at most $|x|+1$; moreover there are a scan state $st$ and register values $R$
such that $st$ is the scan of the first $W(2s+1)$ bits of $w$, every register of $R$ is
at most $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, and $R_A=2|x|+2$, $R_S=s$, $R_T=0$, and $R_{Pos}$ is the value
of those following bits. The codec register program, started at its length-scan label
with all registers zero and run with its two membership oracles on input $y$, can reach
its completion label with state $st$ and registers $R$, while throughout the run its
configuration satisfies the program’s precondition and every register remains at most
$(8W+8)(|y|+1)$. Or else every representation $y=\langle x,\langle
w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ satisfying the stated bit-length bound fails the
stated length, marker-bit, or payload-value checks, and the same program, from the same
initial configuration and under the same register bound and precondition, halts with
answer false.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Equality of Boolean Indicators]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.indicator_eq_of_iff}
\label{Complexity.Codec.indicator_eq_of_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings, let $y$ be a bit string, and let $P$ be a
decidable proposition. If $y$ belongs to $L$ exactly when $P$ holds, then the Boolean
indicator of $L$ at $y$ equals the Boolean truth value of $P$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Shape of a configuration code]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.shape_of_code}
\label{Complexity.Codec.shape_of_code}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Suppose $y=\langle
x,\langle\operatorname{bits}(c),\operatorname{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$. If a machine
configuration on input $x$ has code $c$ at scale $s$, then $y$ has the asserted shape:
it has that pairing form, and the length of the binary representation of $s$ is at most
the length of the binary representation of $y$'s length.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Initial scan state]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.InitScan}
\label{Complexity.Codec.InitScan}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.VAcc, Complexity.Codec.VSt}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$st$ be a verifier state for $N$. The initial-scan predicate holds exactly when $st$ is
an accepting verifier state, its head-position component is the initial machine state at
tape position $0$, and its final Boolean component is true.
\end{definition}

Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and
write $y$ for the paired encoding of $x$ and the paired encoding of $w$ and $r$. Let
$R$ be a register assignment, $s$ a natural number, and $st$ a verifier-and-accumulator
